# Session-scoped CDP access

Status: Draft

## Outcome

`cloakbrowser-mcp` can optionally expose the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP)
endpoint of the browser already owned by an MCP session. The endpoint is an
escape hatch for external low-level clients; it does not replace or extend the
deterministic upstream Playwright MCP tool surface.

Each MCP session continues to own one independent upstream Playwright MCP and
browser runtime. A CDP-enabled session additionally owns one internal Chromium
loopback endpoint, one bridge-managed external HTTP/WebSocket proxy, and one
external port lease for its complete lifetime. Repeated MCP requests and
multiple CDP client connections within that session reuse those resources.
They are not created per request or per CDP connection.

The feature is opt-in, supports the existing `cloak` and `playwright` browser
engines, works through stdio and multi-session Streamable HTTP, and is available
in direct Node package and Docker execution.

## Control-surface boundary

The existing Playwright MCP tools remain the structured surface for bounded,
schema-defined browser operations. The bridge MUST forward those tools without
copying, rewriting, or adding CDP commands to their contracts.

CDP is a separate, lower-level HTTP/WebSocket control surface for clients that
need protocol domains, target events, tracing, debugging, instrumentation, or
third-party integrations not represented by MCP tools. CDP permits arbitrary
commands and asynchronous events; therefore callers, not the bridge, own
coordination of conflicting MCP and CDP operations.

No new local MCP tool is added. `cloakbrowser_bridge_info` is extended to
describe the current session's managed CDP endpoint.

## Architecture and ownership

```text
MCP session
  -> session-owned upstream Playwright MCP child
  -> session-owned Chromium browser runtime
     -> internal loopback CDP endpoint on an implementation-owned port
  -> session-owned bridge HTTP/WebSocket proxy
     -> external port leased from the configured pool
     -> external CDP clients
```

For stdio, the process has one MCP session and one browser runtime. For
Streamable HTTP, every admitted MCP session has its own upstream child, browser
runtime, optional CDP proxy, and optional external port lease. The proxy may run
inside the outer bridge process; it is not required to be a separate operating
system process. A Chromium runtime may itself contain browser, renderer, GPU,
and utility subprocesses.

Chromium's own remote-debugging server remains loopback-only. The bridge MUST
NOT depend on `--remote-debugging-address` exposing it externally. Remote access
is provided only by the session-owned proxy.

## Public configuration

The managed feature uses the bridge-specific `CLOAK_PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_*`
namespace:

- `--cdp-port-range <port|start-end>` /
  `CLOAK_PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_CDP_PORT_RANGE` configures the external port pool. One
  integer denotes a one-port pool. Omitting it disables managed CDP globally.
- `--cdp-host <host>` / `CLOAK_PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_CDP_HOST` configures the proxy
  bind host and defaults to `127.0.0.1`.
- `--cdp-allow-remote` / `CLOAK_PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_CDP_ALLOW_REMOTE=true` is
  required when the bind host is not loopback. It defaults to false.
- `--cdp-advertised-host <host>` /
  `CLOAK_PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_CDP_ADVERTISED_HOST` optionally replaces the host used
  in discovery output. It does not replace the leased port.
- Streamable HTTP initialize metadata under
  `io.github.swimmwatch/cloakbrowser-mcp` accepts the flat camelCase boolean
  `cdpEnabled` as a per-session override.

When a port range is configured, managed CDP is enabled by default for stdio
and for Streamable HTTP sessions. An HTTP session can set `cdpEnabled: false`
and consume no CDP resources. `cdpEnabled: true` without a configured port pool
is invalid. The existing global configuration is the default and initialize
metadata has precedence only for its session.

The advertised URL always retains the session's leased proxy port. Docker,
NAT, and reverse-proxy deployments MUST map CDP ports one-to-one if they rely on
the advertised URL. Arbitrary external port remapping is not part of this
version.

## Requirements

### CDP-001: Opt-in configuration and validation

Managed CDP MUST remain disabled when no port range is configured. A configured
range MUST parse strictly as one decimal port or one inclusive ascending
`start-end` range whose values are within `1..65535`. Whitespace, empty bounds,
descending ranges, duplicate separators, non-decimal values, and out-of-range
values MUST fail with an actionable configuration error.

CDP-related host values MUST be non-empty and valid for their documented role.
An advertised host MUST contain no scheme, path, query, fragment, credentials,
or port. IPv6 formatting in returned URLs MUST be unambiguous. A wildcard bind
host such as `0.0.0.0` or `::` MUST never be emitted as a connectable URL.

Non-loopback binding MUST fail unless the separate remote opt-in is enabled.
The first version provides no built-in TLS or authentication. Enabling remote
access MUST produce an operator-visible warning on stderr that identifies the
unauthenticated privileged control surface without exposing browser state or
credentials.

#### Acceptance

- CLI and environment parsing accept the documented single-port and range
  forms and reject invalid forms before launching an upstream child.
- Default startup creates no CDP proxy, internal remote-debugging endpoint, or
  port lease.
- Loopback binding needs no remote opt-in; wildcard, private, public, and other
  non-loopback binds do.
- `cdpEnabled: false` disables CDP for one HTTP session even when the global
  range is configured; `cdpEnabled: true` cannot invent a missing pool.

### CDP-002: Session ownership and isolation

Every CDP-enabled MCP session MUST own exactly one upstream Playwright MCP
child, one browser runtime, one internal CDP endpoint, one external proxy, and
one external port lease. MCP requests within a session and any number of
supported CDP client connections reuse that session state. A new MCP session
MUST NOT attach to another session's browser or proxy.

The CDP endpoint MUST expose the same browser runtime controlled by the MCP
tools: the same contexts, pages, cookies, storage, configured proxy, fingerprint,
extensions, and persistent or isolated profile semantics. The implementation
MUST NOT launch a second browser solely for CDP.

#### Acceptance

- Two simultaneous HTTP sessions receive different leased ports and different
  Chromium runtimes; a page, cookie, or storage mutation in one is absent from
  the other.
- A page created or mutated through MCP is observable through that session's
  CDP endpoint and vice versa.
- Multiple CDP clients can connect to one session without creating another
  upstream child, browser runtime, or port lease.
- Stdio has one session-scoped endpoint and does not introduce an HTTP-style
  session registry.

### CDP-003: Browser launch and internal endpoint

The bridge MUST configure Chromium remote debugging on a distinct internal
loopback port before connecting the session's upstream Playwright MCP. Browser
startup remains part of upstream initialization and MUST NOT be deferred until
the first browser tool call.

The internal endpoint MUST never bind a non-loopback interface, be advertised
to clients, or consume the external public port lease. The browser launch MUST
retain Playwright MCP's existing isolated or persistent context behavior and
an explicit non-default session profile as required by Chrome 136 and later.
The bridge MUST NOT add `--remote-allow-origins=*`.

Internal port selection and discovery are implementation-owned. They MUST be
bounded, collision-safe within the bridge process, verify that the discovered
endpoint belongs to the session's browser, and fail closed rather than attach
the proxy to an unrelated process.

#### Acceptance

- Process/socket inspection shows Chromium CDP listening only on loopback and
  the proxy listening separately on the leased external port.
- Both `cloak` and `playwright` engines reach CDP readiness during session
  initialization with isolated and configured persistent profile cases.
- An occupied or substituted internal endpoint cannot make the bridge proxy an
  unrelated browser.
- Browser launch arguments contain neither a managed non-loopback debugging
  address nor a wildcard remote-origin allowance.

### CDP-004: Deterministic external port leasing

The bridge MUST maintain one process-wide allocator for the configured external
pool. It MUST select the lowest port not currently leased by another managed
session, reserve it atomically across concurrent admissions, and retain the
lease until session cleanup completes.

After selecting the candidate, any operating-system bind conflict MUST fail
that session's initialization immediately. The allocator MUST NOT skip an
externally occupied candidate and try a later port. Exhausting the pool also
fails initialization. Failed initialization releases any provisional lease;
normal session closure makes the port available for a later session.

#### Acceptance

- Concurrent admissions cannot receive the same port.
- Active managed sessions consume ports in ascending order while non-CDP
  sessions consume none.
- If the next candidate is occupied externally, initialization fails even when
  a later range port is free.
- Pool exhaustion returns a distinct actionable error without disturbing
  existing sessions.
- After complete cleanup, a later session can deterministically reuse the
  lowest released port.

### CDP-005: HTTP/WebSocket-aware proxy

Every CDP-enabled runtime MUST expose a bridge-owned HTTP/WebSocket-aware reverse
proxy on its leased port. A transparent TCP forwarder is insufficient.

After security validation, the proxy MUST preserve standard Chromium DevTools
HTTP discovery and control paths and bidirectionally relay browser- and
target-level WebSocket connections, including text/binary frames, close codes,
backpressure, and disconnects. It MUST rewrite all returned connectable
WebSocket debugger URLs to the current advertised external authority while
preserving target identifiers and paths. It MUST NOT expose the internal port
or add unrelated `cloakserve` endpoints.

The proxy's upstream HTTP requests MUST use a loopback `Host`; upstream
WebSocket handshakes MUST omit `Origin`. Client-supplied forwarding headers MUST
NOT override the chosen internal authority.

#### Acceptance

- `/json/version`, `/json/version/`, `/json`, and `/json/list` return usable
  discovery documents whose WebSocket URLs reference the external host and
  leased port only.
- Playwright `chromium.connectOverCDP()` works with the advertised HTTP
  discovery URL and with a rewritten browser WebSocket URL.
- Browser- and page-target CDP traffic remains bidirectional under concurrent
  messages and large frames without unbounded buffering.
- Closing either side closes its paired connection without terminating other
  clients or the owning MCP session.

### CDP-006: Host and Origin policy

The proxy MUST enforce a strict derived policy without a public Origin
allowlist. Incoming `Host` MUST match an allowed bind or advertised authority
for the session's leased port. Missing, malformed, mismatched, or wildcard
authorities MUST be rejected before forwarding.

WebSocket requests without `Origin` MUST be accepted for non-browser CDP
clients after Host validation. When `Origin` is present, its authority MUST
match an allowed endpoint authority. The bridge MUST NOT silently convert an
arbitrary incoming Origin into an allowed upstream Origin.

Hosted DevTools from a different web origin is not directly supported in this
version; an operator may place a separately secured same-origin reverse proxy
in front of the endpoint.

#### Acceptance

- Accepted advertised and direct loopback authorities work for HTTP and
  WebSocket clients.
- DNS-rebinding-style Host values and cross-origin browser WebSocket attempts
  receive a bounded rejection and never reach Chromium.
- Programmatic clients that omit Origin continue to work.
- Rejection diagnostics do not disclose internal ports, target identifiers,
  cookies, page URLs, or credentials.

### CDP-007: Readiness and initialization failure

A CDP-enabled MCP initialization MUST complete only after all of the following
are true within a bounded deadline:

1. the external port is leased and bound by the session proxy;
2. the upstream child and browser runtime are initialized;
3. the internal loopback CDP endpoint belongs to that browser and responds;
4. the external proxy's `/json/version` responds with a usable rewritten
   `webSocketDebuggerUrl`.

Before readiness, the proxy MUST NOT forward client traffic or advertise an
endpoint. Any timeout, early browser exit, internal discovery error, proxy bind
failure, or invalid discovery response MUST fail initialization and clean up
all partially created session resources. Clients are not required to retry an
eventually ready endpoint after successful initialize.

#### Acceptance

- Successful initialize is immediately followed by successful discovery and a
  WebSocket connection without polling.
- Injected failures at every startup phase produce no active MCP session,
  proxy listener, upstream child, browser, temporary resource, or retained port
  lease.
- One failing HTTP admission does not stop or reassign another active session.

### CDP-008: Session discovery

`cloakbrowser_bridge_info` MUST preserve its current fields and add a `cdp`
object for the calling MCP session.

When managed CDP is disabled, the object is `{ "enabled": false }`. When it is
enabled and ready, it contains:

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "bindHost": "0.0.0.0",
  "port": 9222,
  "advertisedHost": "cloakbrowser-mcp",
  "discoveryUrl": "http://cloakbrowser-mcp:9222"
}
```

`advertisedHost` is nullable when none is configured. `discoveryUrl` uses the
advertised host when present, otherwise a non-wildcard bind host. It MUST be
null when no connectable host can be determined. `port` always remains the
leased proxy port. The tool MUST NOT expose the internal endpoint or transient
browser/target WebSocket identifiers.

#### Acceptance

- Calls from different HTTP sessions return their own enabled state, port, and
  URL.
- Wildcard bind without an advertised host returns separate bind/port data and
  `discoveryUrl: null`, never `http://0.0.0.0:...` or an equivalent wildcard.
- IPv4, IPv6, and hostname URL formatting is valid and deterministic.
- The local tool count and names remain unchanged.

### CDP-009: Lifecycle and destructive external actions

The MCP session remains the sole owner of the browser lifecycle. A normal CDP
client disconnect MUST NOT close the browser or MCP session. Closing or expiring
the MCP session MUST stop accepting CDP traffic, close active proxied sockets,
dispose the upstream/browser runtime, release temporary resources, and only
then release the external port lease.

An external `Browser.close` command is an unsupported destructive action. If it
terminates the browser, the bridge MUST NOT auto-restart it or claim that the
same MCP/CDP session has been preserved. Subsequent operations fail clearly and
the caller creates a new MCP session for recovery.

#### Acceptance

- Repeated CDP connect/disconnect cycles leave MCP browser operations usable.
- MCP DELETE, idle expiry, stdio shutdown, signals, and startup rollback each
  close proxy connections and release the correct port exactly once.
- Browser termination through CDP causes no hidden replacement browser and no
  reassignment of the endpoint to another runtime.
- Shutdown races cannot admit a new connection or release a port while an old
  proxy connection can still reach the closing browser.

### CDP-010: Concurrent MCP and CDP control

MCP and CDP clients MAY operate concurrently on the same session browser. The
bridge MUST NOT serialize arbitrary browser commands, infer intent, or add a
cross-protocol transaction/locking API. Callers own ordering when operations can
conflict.

Independent observations and non-conflicting operations MUST remain usable.
The bridge MUST preserve Chromium CDP events and command responses without
translating them into MCP events or tool results.

#### Acceptance

- A CDP event subscriber observes navigation or target creation initiated by
  MCP.
- Non-conflicting concurrent MCP and CDP reads complete without global
  cross-session blocking.
- Tests document that conflicting navigation, page closure, input, or storage
  mutations have caller-controlled outcomes rather than a bridge guarantee.

### CDP-011: Raw Chromium argument compatibility

Managed CDP configuration MUST reject
`CLOAK_PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_EXTRA_ARGS` entries for
`--remote-debugging-port` or `--remote-debugging-address`, including supported
assignment variants, before browser launch. The bridge MUST NOT silently
override or duplicate them.

Without managed CDP configuration, existing raw argument pass-through remains
unchanged for compatibility. Such unmanaged endpoints receive no allocation,
proxying, validation, readiness, lifecycle, or `cloakbrowser_bridge_info`
guarantee and are reported as managed CDP disabled.

#### Acceptance

- Dedicated configuration plus either conflicting raw flag fails with the
  offending flag name but without dumping all environment values.
- Raw flags without the dedicated port range still reach the existing launch
  path exactly as before.
- Both browser engines apply the same conflict rule.

### CDP-012: Platform and protocol compatibility

The feature MUST work for direct Node package execution and the published
Docker `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` images, with both `cloak` and `playwright`
engines and both MCP transports. It MUST preserve Streamable HTTP session
isolation, authentication, TLS, capacity, idle cleanup, and health behavior.

The implementation MUST NOT mutate upstream Playwright MCP browser tool
schemas, add a Playwright Server protocol gateway, or claim that CDP satisfies
clients expecting Playwright `chromium.connect()`.

#### Acceptance

- Existing bridge parity, unit, integration, packaged CLI, and Docker checks
  pass without weakened assertions.
- The same public configuration and discovery shape works in Node and Docker.
- The current Open WebUI `chromium.connect(PLAYWRIGHT_WS_URL)` flow remains an
  explicit non-goal; clients must use a CDP-capable connection method.

### CDP-013: Logging and operational safety

Runtime logs and proxy diagnostics MUST remain off stdout. Errors and warnings
go to stderr through existing redaction and logging policy. Normal operation
MUST NOT log full discovery documents, WebSocket target IDs, CDP payloads,
cookies, page contents, proxy credentials, or profile paths.

The bridge MUST bound startup waits, HTTP header/body handling, WebSocket
handshakes, shutdown, and error responses. Slow or malformed CDP clients MUST
NOT block MCP processing, allocator progress, other sessions, or cleanup.

#### Acceptance

- Stdio stdout contains only MCP protocol messages under successful, rejected,
  and failed CDP connections.
- Remote opt-in warning and allocation/readiness errors are actionable and
  contain no protected runtime data.
- Malformed HTTP, invalid upgrades, oversized headers/frames, slow peers, and
  abrupt disconnects have bounded resource use and session-local effects.

### CDP-014: Verification coverage

Automated coverage MUST include parsers and precedence, allocator concurrency,
proxy URL rewriting, Host/Origin policy, readiness failures, discovery shape,
lifecycle races, and real-browser state sharing. Fake-upstream coverage remains
for deterministic MCP proxy behavior, but it is not sufficient evidence for
the Chromium or CDP boundary.

#### Acceptance

- Unit/property tests cover valid and invalid range/host/metadata combinations,
  raw-flag conflicts, URL formatting, and allocator invariants.
- Integration tests cover simultaneous HTTP sessions, one CDP-disabled session,
  occupied candidate, exhaustion, release/reuse, startup rollback, and shutdown
  with active WebSockets.
- Real-browser Node and Docker tests connect a CDP-capable client, verify MCP/CDP
  shared state, verify cross-session isolation, and exercise both browser
  engines across the supported transport matrix without assuming one fixed
  machine port.
- Security tests prove rejected Host/Origin requests never reach Chromium and
  non-loopback binding requires the explicit opt-in.
- Final implementation validation runs `npm run check` plus the smallest
  relevant packaged CLI, Docker build/smoke, and real-browser CDP checks.

### CDP-015: Operator documentation

Public configuration, Docker, tools, and security documentation MUST explain
how to enable managed CDP, allocate and publish a port range, use
`cdpEnabled`, configure an advertised host, and connect with an HTTP discovery
URL. It MUST distinguish CDP from the Playwright Server protocol and explain
that remote CDP is unauthenticated privileged browser control.

Documentation MUST describe one-to-one Docker port publication, per-session
port ownership, `bridge_info` discovery, unsupported `Browser.close`, caller
coordination, wildcard URL behavior, raw-argument limitations, and the lack of
built-in TLS/authentication.

#### Acceptance

- Examples cover stdio Node, multi-session Streamable HTTP, and Docker with a
  range large enough for the configured session capacity.
- Examples use CDP-capable clients such as Playwright
  `chromium.connectOverCDP()` and do not present current Open WebUI direct
  compatibility as working.
- Every affected localized page is updated consistently and documentation,
  SEO, compatibility, and translation-manifest checks pass.

## Failure recovery and rollback

- A configuration or readiness failure rejects only the new CDP-enabled HTTP
  session where session isolation permits. Stdio startup fails because no
  independent session remains available.
- Operators recover pool exhaustion by closing sessions or configuring a pool
  large enough for the intended concurrent CDP-enabled session count.
- Operators recover external port collision by freeing the deterministic next
  candidate or changing the configured pool; the bridge does not scan past it.
- Operators recover destructive browser closure or unexpected browser exit by
  creating a new MCP session. There is no in-place browser restart.
- Disabling or rolling back the feature removes managed CDP endpoints without a
  stored-data migration. Existing unmanaged raw Chromium flags retain their
  prior unsupported behavior.

## Non-goals

- Replacing, wrapping, or expanding upstream Playwright MCP browser tools.
- Adding a generic CDP-command MCP tool or project-owned CDP schema.
- Implementing a Playwright Server-compatible WebSocket gateway.
- Direct compatibility with current Open WebUI code that calls
  `chromium.connect()`.
- Built-in CDP TLS, authentication, authorization, per-command policy, audit
  logging, or hostile-tenant isolation.
- Automatic external port remapping, service discovery, load balancing, or
  cross-process port coordination.
- A configurable WebSocket Origin allowlist or direct hosted DevTools support
  from an unrelated web origin.
- Preventing an authorized CDP client from issuing destructive protocol
  commands, or transparently recovering from them.
- Adding nonstandard `cloakserve` browser-management endpoints.

## Objective acceptance

The specification is satisfied when an opted-in stdio or Streamable HTTP
session exposes a ready, session-specific, securely routed Chromium CDP
discovery endpoint; MCP and CDP clients observe the same browser state; multiple
HTTP sessions remain isolated and deterministically retain different ports;
cleanup and failure release every owned resource; Node and Docker real-browser
checks pass; and public documentation accurately describes the protocol and
security boundaries.

## Evidence and delivery boundary

- [Issue #134](https://github.com/swimmwatch/cloakbrowser-mcp/issues/134)
  requests optional CDP access and proposes Chromium debugging flags.
- [Chromium remote debugging server](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/chrome/browser/devtools/remote_debugging_server.cc)
  binds current browser CDP servers to loopback addresses.
- [Chromium DevTools HTTP handler](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/master/content/browser/devtools/devtools_http_handler.cc)
  validates Host and WebSocket Origin.
- [Chrome 136 remote-debugging change](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/remote-debugging-port)
  requires a non-default user data directory for remote-debugging switches.
- [Playwright `connectOverCDP`](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/v1.61.0/docs/src/api/class-browsertype.md)
  accepts HTTP discovery or browser WebSocket endpoints and documents lower
  fidelity than the Playwright protocol.
- `src/server.ts` owns one runtime for stdio; `src/http/server.ts` creates and
  disposes one independent runtime per admitted HTTP session.
- `src/bridge/config.ts` owns generated upstream browser configuration;
  `src/http/requests.ts` owns flat camelCase per-session initialize metadata;
  `src/bridge/tools.ts` owns `cloakbrowser_bridge_info`.
- The required planning artifacts are `quality/scenarios.yaml` and
  `architecture/model.dsl`; they are not created by this specification stage.
- This Draft does not authorize implementation, planning, commit, push, pull
  request changes, issue changes, release work, or publication.

profiles.reason: Adds public opt-in CLI, environment, and Streamable HTTP initialize metadata contracts that change Chromium launch behavior.
Adds a bridge-owned per-session HTTP/WebSocket proxy for external Chromium CDP clients and endpoint discovery.
Port pools, internal and external listeners, Docker networking, per-session lifecycle, collisions, readiness, and diagnostics are material.
The proxy exposes privileged unauthenticated browser control and can reveal cookies, pages, and profile state outside MCP authentication.
MCP, bridge proxy, and CDP clients concurrently control and observe the same session-owned browser state.
No visual product interface or user interaction design is added.
No project-owned asynchronous event contract is introduced; CDP events remain Chromium protocol behavior.
No new stored schema or migration is introduced; existing browser profile data remains owned by each browser runtime.

rationale: Deep remains required because this evolves public configuration and initialize metadata, adds a security-critical network proxy, and supports external clients across Node and Docker.
The user confirmed all MCP transport modes including multiple independent Streamable HTTP sessions and both cloak and playwright browser engines.
Current Chromium binds browser CDP only to loopback, so the user selected one bridge-owned external proxy port per CDP-enabled MCP runtime.
A deterministic architecture model is now warranted to map MCP session ownership, browser process, internal CDP endpoint, external proxy endpoint, and cleanup.
Measurable real-browser concurrency, isolation, failure, and security scenarios remain required.
